Field notes · October

Autumn at the footbridge

What we found at the footbridge, and what to do before winter.

The river

The river rose twice that week, and both times the footbridge held. The second rise came within a hand of the deck boards, which is closer than any year since the bridge was rebuilt.

We recommend raising the deck by one course before the spring melt. The cost is modest and the work can be done in two days with the water low.

MLMaya Lindqvist5m ago

Two days is optimistic. Last time the same job took a week; say so, or give a range.

The path

The path on the north bank is washed out for about twenty metres. Walkers are cutting across the meadow, which is doing more harm than the river did.

This screen

Reply, react, or change your mind

Open in prototypereview.html#answer-a-thread

Let Maya answer a thread in place: reply beneath the comment, react with one emoji, or open the More menu to copy, edit or delete her own comment.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya reads her comment back and wants to soften it with a second thought. She also wants to know what the three small icons at the card's top right do.

Content
  • The page with her thread open beside the second paragraph, the tag reading 1.
  • On the open card, the three actions showing: React, Resolve and More. More is pressed (default): its menu is open under it with Copy thread, Edit and Delete. The reply box holds "Or give a range: two days with the water low, a week otherwise."
  • After Reply (success): the reply sits indented beneath the comment with her avatar, name and "just now"; the reply box is empty again; React was pressed and the quick row of five emoji shows under the comment, with 👍 1 already given.
Wording
  • {emoji} {n} a reaction given, with how many gave it.
  • Thread by {name} the card's accessible name.
  • {time} · edited the time of a comment whose words were changed.
  • Delete this comment? the title of the second question before Delete, in a dialog with Cancel and Delete.
  • Nothing is left in its place. the dialog's one line.
  • It has no replies. the dialog's meta line when the thread has none.
  • Its {n} replies go with it. the dialog's meta line when it has replies ("Its 1 reply goes with it.").
  • Reply discarded. after Cancel in a reply box with words in it.
Components
Comment card openPopover menu iconAvatar smButton primary, quietChip filterComment control cornerIcon button quietText field
States
  • EmptyNot applicable
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorNot applicable
Interactions
  • Reply (or Enter in the reply box) sends the reply: it arrives indented beneath the comment with a fade and a short drop over --ds-motion-settle, and the box empties and keeps focus. Every reply is to the original comment: there is no reply to a reply.
  • React opens the quick row under the comment, fading in over --ds-motion-settle; choosing an emoji adds it as a pressed pill with its count (or counts it up) and the quick row fades out. The row closes when its thread does.
  • More opens its menu as any popover menu does: Copy thread puts the whole thread on the clipboard as Markdown (focus stays on ⋯); Edit puts the words back in a box with Cancel and Save, and the edited comment is marked "edited"; Delete asks once more, and deleting the first comment removes the whole thread.
Show 2 more
  • Resolve fades the thread and its highlight away.
  • Esc closes the menu first, then the thread.
Requirements
  • FR-009 Every thread takes replies one level deep beneath the comment, reactions as a quick row of five emoji that become counted pills, and a More menu with Copy thread, and on the writer's own comment Edit and Delete, where Delete asks once more.
Acceptance criteria
  1. AC-answer-a-thread-1FR-009PassedGiven her thread open, when Maya types a reply and presses Enter, then the reply appears indented beneath the comment with her name and "just now", and the reply box is empty with focus still in it.
  2. AC-answer-a-thread-2FR-009PassedGiven her thread open, when she presses React and chooses 👍, then "👍 1" shows under the comment and the quick row goes.
  3. AC-answer-a-thread-3FR-009PassedGiven her thread open, when she presses More, then a menu shows Copy thread, Edit and Delete in that order, and Esc closes it with focus back on More.
  4. AC-answer-a-thread-4FR-009PassedGiven the More menu open, when she chooses Delete and confirms, then the thread and its card are gone and the tag's count falls by one.Set up: the read-thread screen, then More.

Delete a comment, asked once more

Let Maya delete a comment of her own, with one second question so a slip never loses a thread.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya left a comment on the wrong paragraph and wants it gone, replies and all, without a trace.

Content
  • The page with her thread open beside the second paragraph and the More menu's Delete pressed.
  • A dialog over the page (default): "Delete this comment?", the meta line "It has no replies." (or "Its {n} replies go with it."), one line "Nothing is left in its place.", and Cancel and Delete, Delete in the danger look.
  • After Delete (success): the card is gone from the column, nothing marks where it was, and the tag shows the comment mark again, with no count.
Wording
  • It has no replies. the dialog's meta line when the thread has none.
  • Its {n} replies go with it. when it has replies ("Its 1 reply goes with it.").
Components

States

  • LoadingNot applicable

Interactions
  • Delete in the More menu opens the dialog, which fades and settles in over --ds-motion-settle with focus on Cancel; Esc, Cancel or a click on the dimmed page closes it with nothing changed, focus back on More.
  • Delete in the dialog closes it and fades the card out over --ds-motion-settle; deleting a thread's first comment removes the whole thread, replies and all. A deleted reply goes alone.
  • The second question can never be answered by the same double-click or double tap that asked it.
Requirements
  • FR-013 Deleting a comment asks once more in a dialog that says what goes with it; a deleted comment leaves nothing in its place, and deleting a thread's first comment removes the whole thread.
Acceptance criteria

  2. AC-delete-a-thread-2FR-013PassedGiven the dialog, when she presses Esc, then it closes, the thread is still there and focus is on More.
  3. AC-delete-a-thread-3FR-013PassedGiven the dialog, when she presses Delete, then the card is gone, no mark is left beside the paragraph and the tag shows no count.

Resolve a thread, and bring it back

Open in prototypereview.html#resolve-a-thread

Let Maya mark a thread as dealt with so it steps out of the way, and bring it back if it was too soon.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Her colleague has answered and the point is settled; Maya wants the card out of the column but not lost.

Content
  • The page with her thread at rest beside the second paragraph, its actions showing (default): React, Resolve, More.
  • After Resolve (success): the card and the paragraph's highlight have faded away, the tag's count has fallen by one, and a message beside the tag reads "Resolved." for a moment. The thread is still reachable in All comments with ✓ Resolved on, where Reopen brings it back.
Wording
  • Resolved. beside the tag after Resolve, for a few seconds.
  • Reopened. beside the tag after Reopen.
Components
Comment cardPopover menu iconAvatar smButton quietComment control cornerHighlightIcon button quietInline alert successPin
States
  • EmptyNot applicable
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorNot applicable
Interactions
  • Resolve fades the thread's card and its highlight or pin away over --ds-motion-settle; the cards below glide up into the room it leaves. Resolved threads are left out of every copy.
  • After Resolve, the card that moves into its place shows its actions only once the pointer moves, so a second click never resolves a different thread.
  • Reopen, on a resolved card in All comments, brings the card and its mark back with a fade over --ds-motion-settle.
Requirements
  • FR-014 Resolve takes a thread and its mark off the page and out of every copy, with a message beside the control; the thread stays reachable in All comments with Resolved on, where Reopen brings it back.
Acceptance criteria
  1. AC-resolve-a-thread-1FR-014PassedGiven her thread at rest, when Maya presses Resolve, then the card and the paragraph's mark are gone, the tag's count falls by one and "Resolved." shows beside the tag.
  2. AC-resolve-a-thread-2FR-014PassedGiven a resolved thread, when she copies as Markdown, then the thread is not in the text.
  3. AC-resolve-a-thread-3FR-014PassedGiven a resolved thread and All comments open with Resolved on, when she presses Reopen on it, then the card is back beside its paragraph and the tag's count rises by one.Set up: the read-thread screen, Esc, then Resolve; then All comments with Resolved on.
Prompt for this screen

This journey

Manage a thread

Maya answers a thread she started: replies beneath it, reacts, edits or deletes her comment, and resolves or reopens the thread.

Goal
Maya keeps a thread she started in good order: a second thought as a reply, a reaction, a corrected comment, a deleted slip, and a thread resolved once it is dealt with.
Trigger
She reads her own comment back and wants to soften it, or her colleague has answered and the point is settled.
Outcome
The thread says what she means, with its replies and reactions, and threads that are settled are out of the way but can be brought back.
Success
A reply, a reaction, an edit, a delete and a resolve each take one press from the open card, and none loses words typed elsewhere. Nothing is deleted without a second question, and a resolved thread can always be reopened.
Persona
MLMaya Lindqvist
